change_rule: Any change to a field below is a new scenario revision (SCN_FLOATCITY_COASTAL_02 ...), recorded in concept/SCENARIO_CONTRACT.md with the reason. Values are never changed to make a design pass.
documentary_title: Could We Build an Entire City That Floats?

classes.ESTABLISHED_FACT: reported by a source (claim id in research/sources.json)
classes.CALCULATED_ESTIMATE: computed by analysis/design_model.py from facts and assumptions
classes.DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: chosen by the Studio for this scenario; not a fact about any real place
classes.SPECULATIVE_PROPOSAL: what a developer or concept study proposes
classes.UNVERIFIED: not confirmed from a primary source

scenario_type.value: Shore-connected floating extension of an existing coastal city, built in phases from one platform to a neighbourhood to a district.
scenario_type.basis: Owner's preferred starting hypothesis; the only scale with built precedents nearby in kind (CLM_010, CLM_020). Studies place even large concepts in sheltered, limited-fetch water (CLM_050).

proposed_population.basis: Scenario target given in the brief, reached in three phases (A: one platform, B: neighbourhood, C: district). Not a requirement of any real project. For scale: Schoonschip has a little more than 100 residents (CLM_011); OCEANIX Busan was proposed for 12,000 residents and visitors (CLM_031).

site_type.value: Sheltered bay or harbour basin with limited fetch: headlands or existing coastal structures block ocean swell; only short, locally generated waves reach the site in normal conditions.
site_type.basis: CLM_050 (concept study's ideal site), CLM_048 (site selection criteria), CLM_051 (floating breakwaters may not stop long waves).

distance_from_shore.basis: The first platform touches the quay; the district reaches up to about 0.8 km out, within walking distance and reach of link-span bridges (CLM_031 uses link-span bridges to land). Chosen for the story, not from a site study.

water_depth.basis: Deep enough below a ~3 m draft for clearance at low water; shallow enough that the first phases can be held by piles. Deeper water means longer lines and deeper anchors at rising cost (CLM_054). Site survey required.

water_density.basis: Design value used in TU Delft offshore course material (CLM_004). A textbook gives 1,030 kg/m3 for sea water at 0 °C (CLM_008); the 0.5% difference does not change any conclusion.

representative_waves.value: Fetch-limited wind sea inside the basin; ocean swell excluded by site choice. No design wave height or period is fixed at concept stage.
representative_waves.basis: Wave heights and periods must come from site metocean data. The film shows motion only as 'Conceptual motion visualization — not a hydrodynamic simulation' and never quotes amplitudes.

wind_and_storm.value: The region has occasional severe storms with strong winds and raised water levels (storm surge). The design must keep people safe through them; it is not assumed that nothing is damaged.
wind_and_storm.basis: Brief section 6.6; residents feel motion in storms even in sheltered Amsterdam (CLM_022). No return period or wind speed is chosen at concept stage.

tidal_and_water_level_range.basis: Illustrative range of water level (tide plus surge allowance) used only to show why platforms slide on piles and why shore bridges must hinge (analysis: link-span slope). Floating structures follow water level (CLM_041).

seabed.value: Soft sediment (sand or clay) of unknown thickness over firmer ground; suitable for driven piles and embedded anchors, subject to a geotechnical survey.
seabed.basis: Mooring cost depends mainly on bathymetry and seabed (CLM_054). The film names no anchor type as sized.

connection_to_shore.value: Hinged link-span bridges for pedestrians, bicycles and light service and emergency vehicles; utility lines run along them. Water taxis and ferries between platforms.
connection_to_shore.basis: CLM_031 (link-span bridges in the Busan proposal), CLM_023 (waterproof cables and pumps to land), CLM_015 (jetty carrying infrastructure).

construction_technology.value: Reinforced-concrete pontoon hulls with internal watertight compartments, cast in a dock or on a quay and towed to site; low-rise buildings with light timber or steel frames on top.
construction_technology.basis: Precedent: Schoonschip concrete floats built on the quay and towed (CLM_012, CLM_014); concrete hull as counterweight (CLM_021).

value.buildings: timber or light steel frame, low-rise (2–4 storeys) to keep the centre of gravity low

materials.basis: Chloride-induced corrosion of reinforcement in sea water (CLM_059) is a maintenance driver for concrete hulls.

available_external_energy.value: Grid connection to the city through the link-span bridges; rooftop solar and batteries on the platforms reduce, but do not replace, grid supply.
available_external_energy.basis: Precedent: Schoonschip has solar, batteries and one shared grid connection (CLM_016). The film does not claim self-sufficiency.

water_supply.value: Drinking water from the city mains along the bridges; rainwater collection for non-potable use. No desalination in the base case.
water_supply.basis: Shore-connected scenario (CLM_043: connect to land or develop off-grid alternatives).

wastewater.value: Grey and black water collected separately and pumped to treatment on land.
wastewater.basis: CLM_017 (separation at Schoonschip), CLM_023 (pumps to municipal services).

food_supply.value: From land, as for any city district. No food autonomy target.
food_supply.basis: Local food production dominates the energy demand of an autonomous concept (CLM_058); the scenario avoids that requirement.

emergency_access.value: Every platform has two independent routes to land (bridge or neighbouring platform) and a landing for fire and rescue boats; shelter-in-place spaces on each neighbourhood platform.
emergency_access.basis: Brief section 6.6–6.7; no fire code is claimed as met.

value: House 10,000 residents in phases, each phase usable on its own.
Keep homes where motion is smallest; put services and open space where larger motion is tolerated (CLM_055).
Every module, connector and mooring element inspectable and replaceable.
Shore-connected utilities, public access to the waterfront, no gated enclave (CLM_046).

module_geometry_assumptions.basis: Chosen to be plausible for a concept sketch and varied in the sensitivity runs; none is a measured or code value. Concept only — no structural design.

value: open-ocean or offshore siting (shown only as a counterfactual, Design D)
self-sufficiency in energy, water or food
any claim of structural, mooring, storm or comfort adequacy
ecological effects of shade and hard surfaces (CLM_044)
cost and affordability (no peer-reviewed cost basis; CLM_061)
uncertainties.basis: Each is named in the film's verdict as unresolved at concept stage.
